value.body: Seed, fertiliser and crop-protection (agrochemical) companies hire agriculture graduates for field and sales work, product demonstrations, farmer meetings, dealer management and, at some firms, research, production and quality roles. It is one of the largest private employers of B.Sc Agriculture graduates.

items.label: Key laws
items.value: Seeds Act 1966; Insecticides Act 1968; Fertiliser (Control) Order 1985
items.note: Govern product sale and dealer licensing

items.label: Typical entry roles
items.value: Field / market development officer, territory sales officer, trainee

items.label: B.Agri students enrolled
items.note: All years of the programme, all modes; degrees recorded under other names are not included

items.label: B.Agri pass-outs a year
items.note: Graduates who supply much of the field and sales workforce in this sector
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), institutions that reported

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc Agriculture (or horticulture / related degree). Companies hire through campus placements at agricultural universities and direct recruitment; an MBA in agri-business or an M.Sc can lead to marketing or R&D roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most entry roles are field-based with heavy rural travel and sales targets.
Work peaks with the kharif and rabi seasons.
Growth usually runs from territory to area and regional management, or into product and marketing roles.

value.title: B.Agri enrolment in India
value.note: Counts students across all years of the B.Agri programme, not new admissions or job openings. Programmes reported under other names (such as B.Sc Agriculture) may be counted elsewhere.
